<USER_REQUEST>
Read SPEC_v0.2.md and agent_v1.mjs first. Then create exactly one file, eval.mjs (ES module, no new dependencies, only Node built-ins and the global fetch), and change nothing else.

Purpose: run the 7 eval cases against an agent script and compare its verdict with the pinned expected verdict.

Usage: node eval.mjs agent_v1.mjs (the agent script name is the first argument; default agent_v1.mjs)

Cases (the input is the single argument passed to the agent; always use 127.0.0.1, never localhost):
1 "always-502": http://127.0.0.1:4010/always-502, expected NEEDS_CHECK
2 "no-site-active-social": http://127.0.0.1:4010/case2/social/active, expected QUALIFY
3 "modern-site": http://127.0.0.1:4010/case3/, expected REJECT
4 "outdated-site": http://127.0.0.1:4010/case4/, expected QUALIFY
5 "parked-domain": http://127.0.0.1:4010/case5/, expected REJECT
6 "redirect-to-social": http://127.0.0.1:4010/case6/, expected QUALIFY
7 "intermittent-timeouts": http://127.0.0.1:4010/case7/, expected NEEDS_CHECK

Behavior:
- Before starting, fetch http://127.0.0.1:4010/ok. If it fails or is not 200, print "Fixture server is not running. Start it with: node fixtures\server.js" and exit 1.
- Run the cases in order. Before case 7 only, fetch http://127.0.0.1:4010/__reset.
- For each case run: node --env-file=.env <agent> <input> as a child process (node:child_process spawnSync, process.execPath, timeout 90000 ms, maxBuffer 10 MB). Do not read or print .env.
- Parse the agent's stdout by taking the text from the first "{" to the last "}" and JSON.parse it. If parsing fails, the case verdict is "UNPARSEABLE" and keep the first 200 characters of stdout and stderr in an "error" field.
- From the parsed JSON read verdict, opportunity_score, confidence, reason_code (may be missing) and reason.
- A case passes only when verdict equals expected exactly.
- Wait 10 seconds between cases (not after the last).
- Print a table to the console (case id, name, expected, got, score, confidence, PASS/FAIL) and a final line "Passed X of 7".
- Save results to results/<name>.json and results/<name>.md, where <name> is the agent file name without "agent_" and without ".mjs" (agent_v1.mjs gives v1). Create the results folder if needed. The .md file has the table, the agent name and an ISO timestamp. The .json has the full array of case results.
- Put a short comment at the top of eval.mjs saying the fixtures are simulated.

Do NOT run eval.mjs. Do NOT start the server. Do NOT read or create .env. Do NOT install anything. Do NOT commit. You may run: node --check eval.mjs
</USER_REQUEST>

1: # SignalForge: spec v0.1
2: 
3: ## One line
4: An autonomous agent that investigates a business, verifies whether it really has a weak online presence, and outputs an opportunity brief. Opportunity and confidence are scored separately.
5: 
6: ## Scope (decided)
7: - Not limited to Nigeria. First test niche: interior-design businesses.
8: - Stack: Node.js, Gemini API as the model (Bedrock is not available on the hackathon AWS login), neatlogs for traces, Entire for checkpoints, Crustdata for company data once credits arrive.
9: - No dependency on Agent Orchestrator or AWS.
10: 
11: ## Agent loop
12: 1. INPUT: business name + any known URL or social handle.
13: 2. DISCOVER: find website, social profiles, listings (search + Crustdata when available).
14: 3. PROBE: fetch each asset; record status code, response time, redirect chain, timestamp, and one retry on failure.
15: 4. CLAIMS: model proposes problems (e.g. "no working website", "outdated site", "no booking path"). Each claim must cite an evidence record id.
16: 5. VERIFY: apply the verification policy below. Unsupported claims are dropped or marked UNKNOWN.
17: 6. SCORE: opportunity (0-100) and confidence (0-100), computed separately.
18: 7. OUTPUT: opportunity brief (JSON + readable markdown).
19: 
20: ## Verification policy
21: - A fetch failure (timeout, 5xx, DNS error) is evidence of UNKNOWN, never of "no website". Retry once, then re-check after a delay. Only repeated, consistent failure across checks can support a "site is down" claim, and it still caps confidence.
22: - Every problem claim needs at least one evidence record. No evidence, no claim.
23: - Confidence is capped at 40 when the key claim rests on a single probe.
24: - The model may not raise confidence above what the evidence supports.
25: - Opportunity high + confidence low means "needs human check", not "high opportunity".
26: 
27: ## Output shape
28: ```json
29: {
30:   "business": "",
31:   "claims": [{ "text": "", "evidence_ids": [], "status": "CONFIRMED|INFERRED|UNKNOWN" }],
32:   "evidence": [{ "id": "", "url": "", "status_code": 0, "ms": 0, "checked_at": "" }],
33:   "opportunity": 0,
34:   "confidence": 0,
35:   "recommendation": ""
36: }
37: ```
38: 
39: ## Eval set (7 cases, proposed)
40: 1. Website returns 502 on first probe. v1 wrongly reads it as high opportunity; v2 retries, marks UNKNOWN, caps confidence. This is the demo case.
41: 2. No website, active Instagram with recent posts. Real gap, high confidence.
42: 3. Site loads fine, modern, has booking. Low opportunity.
43: 4. Site loads but is clearly outdated (old copyright year, not mobile-friendly). Medium opportunity, evidence required.
44: 5. Domain parked or expired. High opportunity, confirmed by DNS plus page content.
45: 6. Site only redirects to a Facebook page. Medium opportunity.
46: 7. Slow site (timeouts only on some probes). UNKNOWN, low confidence, recheck.
47: 
48: ## Demo plan
49: Run v1 on case 1, show the neatlogs trace exposing the bad conclusion, add the verification policy, run v2 on all 7 cases, show the before/after table.
50: 
51: ## Open questions
52: - neatlogs integration method (decide after the account exists).
53: - Submission format and end time (check neatlogs.com/hackathon).
54:
